event_name: A Feeling of Itself Opening Reception
newsletter_description: Celebrate the opening of 'A Feeling of Itself' exploring multilingual identity and cultural connection!
description: The opening reception for “A Feeling of Itself” featured a performance by YEIMY (@yeiei.y) and welcome remarks from Lives in Translation students Alma Garcia and Esperanza Santos; Senator M. Teresa Ruiz Senate Majority Leader - District 29; Rutgers University-Newark Chancellor Tonya Smith-Jackson and Provost and Executive Vice Chancellor Jeffrey Robinson; representatives from Lives In Translation; and the lead designers Chantal Fischzang and Gisela Ochoa. The exhibition explores the richness and complexity of living between languages, rooted in the concept of arraigo.
performer: YEIMY, Alma Garcia, Esperanza Santos, Senator M. Teresa Ruiz, Tonya Smith-Jackson, Jeffrey Robinson, Chantal Fischzang, Gisela Ochoa

newsletter_description: Explore the power of language and cultural connection at the 'A Feeling of Itself' exhibition.
description: The exhibition “A Feeling of Itself” explores the richness and complexity of living between languages. Rooted in the concept of arraigo—a sense of belonging shaped through one’s roots—the exhibition layers bilingual interviews, photography, typography, and data visualization to illuminate how translation becomes a powerful form of cultural connection. It asserts language diversity as a source of power, dignity, and collective memory.

This conversation meets you where you are and challenges you to keep going.

Parenting isn't easy, but Jess Hilarious brings humor and honesty to every moment of it. In this candid conversation, she shares the realities of modern Black parenthood. From the highs to the hard days and everything in between. From balancing public life and motherhood to staying grounded in her identity, Jess keeps it real and relatable. Expect laughter, truth, and a reminder that you're not alone in the journey. Come ready to laugh, relate, and leave feeling a little less alone in the journey.

newsletter_description: Experience NEW art by Aly Kourouma exploring material value!
description: Guinea-born, Senegal-raised artist Aly Kourouma (AKA @Timbuctu_State) is opening his newest exhibition “Cosmic Landfill” at @ASG_ArtfullySpaced Gallery! Explore your relationship to material things and question what is value vs. what is disposable with Kourouma’s body of work made with metal, copper, and textiles—all sourced from landfills and junkyards. Artfully Spaced Gallery prioritizes the work of Black artists around the world with many exhibiting artists hailing from the African continent, North America, and right here in Los Angeles!
